references.text: God gives the same blessing to humanity — to be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth — as a direct parallel to the blessing given to sea creatures and birds in verse 22.
After the flood, God commands all animals to leave the ark to multiply and fill the earth, renewing the creation blessing given to them.
God blesses Noah and his sons with the command to be fruitful, repeating the same formula from creation given to sea creatures, birds, and humans.
God repeats the command to be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth, confirming the original creation blessing.
God blesses Jacob with the words 'be fruitful and multiply,' reflecting the original creation blessing first given to sea creatures and birds.
Israel settled in Egypt, were fruitful, and became very numerous — fulfilling God's creation blessing concerning fruitfulness.
Reuse of the creation formula in the promise to Jacob, linking the history of the patriarchs with the foundational principles of creation.
Prophetic restoration of the creation order regarding fruitfulness as part of the final restoration.
The immediate continuation of the creation account, showing the connection between the creation of animals and their provision.
